member.title: User Guide

sections.title: Working Offline and on a Phone (Optional)

member.html:
This guide is for team members: your own list, tasks people share with you, and the optional tools you can use. Team Leaders and managers have their own guides.

01Getting Started

Open hub.totalchb.com on a computer or phone and sign in with your work Google account (@totalchb.com or @kpidriver.com).

  1. Tap Sign In With Google and pick your work account.
  2. Your list, Your Personal Tasks, opens.
  3. The clock beside the logo glows green (Live) while every change is saving for the whole team.
Part of the headerWhat it does
Live clock, beside the logoHub time, Eastern. Every date in the hub uses it. Its colour shows whether your changes are saved (see below); click it for the details
TCHB / KPI DRIVER, in the middleSwitch company boards, each with your % done. You only see the companies you have access to
Active pillHow many people are in the hub now. Click it to see who, and whether on phone or desktop
Sun / moonLight or dark theme; remembered on this device
Your photo or initialsOpens your menu: My Settings, Task Templates, Help and Sign Out

The header stays at the top as you scroll, and the tabs line under the title stays just below it.

Help, in your photo menu, opens this guide inside the hub at any time.

Open and Download at the top of Help give you this guide as a PDF.

Live clockMeaning
Green, glowingLive: connected; every change is saved for everyone
BlueSaving…: a change is on its way
RedNot Saved: a change failed. Click the clock: Retry Now if it is waiting for a connection, otherwise redo the change
GrayLocal Only: saved on this device only; reload to reconnect

Click the clock any time to see when your last change was saved.

02Your List

Everything you need to do is in Your Personal Tasks. You, your Team Leaders and the managers can see it; other members can't.

It holds your own tasks, tasks a Team Leader or manager added for you, and tasks from other lists where you own the task or a subtask. The coloured pill on a task's progress line says where it came from.

Each task card reads left to right: the checkbox, a ring with the % of subtasks done, then the title and who edited it last. Under them is the progress line: a bar with "1 of 4 Subtasks Done", then the task's pills and due date. On the right are the owner, the status, the Details button, the down arrow that opens the subtasks, and the bin.

PillColourMeaning
(no pill)Your own task
Shared by NameGreenFrom someone else's list; you own part of it
Added by MGMTRedA managers' task; you own part of it
Added by Title Commitment AgentGoldMade by the Title Agent; ticking a blocker here ticks it there too
Task Deployment TemplateBlueMade from a task template
CSV Upload TemplateOrangeMade from a CSV file with Upload Tasks

The due date, when set, sits on the same line. It turns redder as the time gets close, and reads Overdue once it passes.

03Working a Task

Add a Task

  1. Type the task in Add a personal task.
  2. Optional: list its subtasks right away. A subtask box appears as you type; press Enter after each one. Each subtask has its own owner button.
  3. Press Add Task (or Enter). The task is yours and joins Not Started.

Status and Ticking

TaskHow its status changes
With subtasksFollows the subtasks: In Progress once one starts, Done when all are done (cancelled ones don't count)
No subtasksTap the status pill and pick Not Started, In Progress, Done or Cancelled
CancelledA cancelled subtask stops counting and the task stays open. To cancel a whole task, tap its status pill and choose Cancel Whole Task: every subtask is cancelled, and Reopen Task brings them back as they were
  • The big checkbox marks the whole task and all its subtasks Done. Unticking sets the done subtasks back to Not Started.
  • The list is grouped In Progress, Not Started, then Done. Drag the six-dot handle to reorder within a group (on a phone, press, hold and slide).
  • Rename a task or subtask by clicking its title. Changes save as you type.

Subtasks

Open a task with its down arrow, then type in Add a subtask and press Enter. On each subtask row:

  • Checkbox sets Done; the status pill picks Not Started, In Progress, Done or Cancelled.
  • Owner pill gives the subtask to someone. The task then shows in their list as Shared by you, and they work only on their own parts.
  • Details (the clipboard) opens the subtask's due date, notes and files.
  • Six-dot handle reorders it; × removes it (see Deleting).

The Buttons on a Task

ButtonWhat it does
Details (clipboard)One panel for Due, Notes, Activity and Files: switch between them with the toggle at its top. It opens on the part you used last. The button shows how many notes and files the task has, and turns red as the due date nears
DuePick a day, hour and minutes (Eastern), then Set Due Date. Remove clears it
NotesWho wrote each and when. Add with Add or Ctrl+Enter. On a task, Include Subtask Notes shows its subtasks' notes too
ActivityEvery change on the task and its subtasks, who made it and when (tasks only)
FilesSwitch between Upload Files (up to 25 MB each) and Add Link (paste a link, name optional). Everyone who can see the task can open them
BinDelete the task (see Deleting)

Under the title, "Edited by" shows who changed the task last. Hover the line to see when it was created, started, done and due.

04Tasks Shared with You

When someone gives you a subtask, or makes you the owner of their task, that task appears in your list marked Shared by them (or Added by MGMT for a managers' task).

  • You see the whole task, so you know how it's going overall.
  • Subtasks owned by others are blurred and can't be clicked, but you can still see whether each is Done, In Progress or Not Started.
  • Your own subtasks work as normal: tick them, set their status and due date, add notes and files.
  • If you own the main task itself, you can work on all of it, including adding subtasks.
  • You can't move, delete or reassign these tasks. Ask the person who shared it, your Team Leader or a manager.
  • Only the parts you own count toward your % (all of it if you own the task).

05Finding Things

ToolWhat it does
Pending (default)Not Started and In Progress together
In Progress / Not Started / DoneOne status only, each with a count
All OwnersPick a person: only tasks they own or have a subtask in. Their subtasks glow green
SearchFinds tasks and subtasks whose words start with what you type, in any case ("ai" finds "AI Review", not "Failsafe"). Matches glow green and tasks open to show matching subtasks
FilesTask Folders: every file and link on the tasks in this view, one folder per task
Expand All / Collapse AllOpen or close every task at once (on a phone, one button does whichever fits)
CancelledCancelled tasks. They leave Pending and don't count toward your %

The filters go back to Pending when you switch company or list. The numbers at the right of the tabs line count tasks fully done, and subtasks done out of all subtasks that count for you; the ring between them is the % done.

06Your Department in Team (Optional)

A manager can let you see your whole department's tasks. When they do, a Team ↔ Personal toggle appears above the add bar.

  • Team shows every personal task in your department, labelled with whose it is, plus MGMT tasks your department owns parts of.
  • You can open and work on these tasks, leave notes and add files.
  • Adding tasks for other people and deleting their tasks stay with Team Leaders and managers.

No toggle? Your view is Personal only; ask a manager if you need the department view.

07Task Templates and Deploy (Optional)

A template is a saved list of subtasks you use again and again. Deploy turns one into a new task in your list, named as you like and tagged Task Deployment template name.

Save a Template

  1. Click your photo or initials (top right) and choose Task Templates.
  2. Press New Template.
  3. Give it a name and type one subtask per line.
  4. Press Save Template. Templates are saved to your account, on every device.

Edit and Delete sit on each template. Deleting a template leaves the tasks already made from it as they are.

Deploy One

  1. Press Deploy beside Add Task (or Deploy on the template in Task Templates) and pick the template.
  2. Name the task and press Deploy.

The task lands in your list, open, with every subtask assigned to you. To add more subtasks from another template later, press Template on the task's progress line.

08Upload Tasks From a CSV (Optional)

Upload Tasks makes one task from a spreadsheet saved as CSV, using your department's upload template. If your department has none yet, the dialog says so.

TemplateDepartmentHow the file is readTask name
SOWTCColumn A becomes the subtasks; columns B and C become each subtask's noteSOW - address
  1. Press Upload Tasks beside Add Task.
  2. Type the property address. The dialog shows the name the task will get.
  3. Choose the CSV file.
  4. Check the switches The file has a header row and The file has a summary row at the bottom (both on by default). Those rows are skipped.
  5. Look over the preview, then press Create Task.

The task goes into your department Team Leader's list, with every subtask assigned to you, so it shows in your list as Shared by them. The CSV is kept in the task's Files & Links, and the task is tagged CSV Upload SOW.

09Deleting Tasks and Removing Subtasks

WhatHowPassword
Your own taskBin, then Undo for 6 seconds if you change your mindNone
A subtask× on the row, then type the password and confirmYour department's subtask password (from your Team Leader)
Shared, MGMT or other people's tasksNo binAsk your Team Leader or a manager

A wrong password shows "That password is not right." Try again. The hub keeps a copy of everything deleted, so ask a manager if something went by mistake.

10Working Offline and on a Phone (Optional)

Working Offline

  1. On the sign-in screen, choose Work Offline In This Browser. The list starts empty and is saved on this device only.
  2. Add tasks, subtasks and notes as usual.
  3. Back online, press Push To Live on a task. That task, with its subtasks and notes, moves into your list (it signs you in first if needed).

Offline tasks left on the device show under an Offline tab until the last one is pushed. Back To Sign In returns to the sign-in screen.

Offline tasks belong to the device, not the person. Anyone using that computer or phone can see and push them.

On a Phone

Everything works the same; the layout stacks so nothing is squeezed.

  • The header is one row: the logo, the Live clock (time only) and your photo. The company tabs sit under it if you have more than one company.
  • Active and Light / Dark are in your photo menu, with Who's Online and its count.
  • Each task card has three parts: the title on top; the progress line (ring, bar, pills and due date); and a footer with the owner, status, Details and the bin.
  • Search, the owner filter, Deploy and Upload Tasks get their own rows. Expand All and Collapse All are one button.
  • Menus, notes and dialogs slide up from the bottom; tap the dimmed area to close.
  • Tip: add the hub to your home screen (Safari: Share, Add to Home Screen; Chrome: menu, Add to Home screen).

11Troubleshooting

ProblemWhat to do
"… isn't on the team list"You used a personal Google account. Sign in with your @totalchb.com or @kpidriver.com account
The sign-in window doesn't appearAllow pop-ups for hub.totalchb.com and try again
I can't click a subtaskIt belongs to someone else on a shared task. You can see its status, but only its owner can change it
A task I expected isn't in my listCheck the company tab and the filter (Pending hides Done). Then ask your Team Leader to check the owner
I don't see the KPI DRIVER tabYou don't have access to that company. Ask Remy
The clock turns red (Not Saved)Your last change didn't save. Click the clock for Retry Now, or reload and redo it
My offline tasks aren't on my other deviceOffline tasks stay on the device they were made on. Push them from there
The page looks oldReload: Ctrl+Shift+R on a computer, pull down on a phone

lead.html:
This guide is for Team Leaders: everything a team member does, plus running your department's tasks. Sections marked optional are tools you can use but don't have to.

01Getting Started

Open hub.totalchb.com on a computer or phone and sign in with your work Google account (@totalchb.com or @kpidriver.com).

  1. Tap Sign In With Google and pick your work account.
  2. The hub opens on Personal, your own list. Team, beside it, holds your department's tasks.
  3. The clock beside the logo glows green (Live) while every change is saving for the whole team.
Part of the headerWhat it does
Live clock, beside the logoHub time, Eastern. Every date in the hub uses it. Its colour shows whether your changes are saved (see below); click it for the details
TCHB / KPI DRIVER, in the middleSwitch company boards, each with your % done. You only see the companies you have access to
Active pillHow many people are in the hub now. Click it to see who, and whether on phone or desktop
Sun / moonLight or dark theme; remembered on this device
Your photo or initialsOpens your menu: My Settings, Task Templates, Help and Sign Out

The header stays at the top as you scroll, and the tabs line under the title stays just below it.

Help, in your photo menu, opens this guide inside the hub at any time, with the delete passwords for the departments you lead.

Open and Download at the top of Help give you this guide as a PDF. Your copy ends with a page of your departments' delete passwords. You can also open the User Guide there, without passwords, to send to a team member.

Live clockMeaning
Green, glowingLive: connected; every change is saved for everyone
BlueSaving…: a change is on its way
RedNot Saved: a change failed. Click the clock: Retry Now if it is waiting for a connection, otherwise redo the change
GrayLocal Only: saved on this device only; reload to reconnect

Click the clock any time to see when your last change was saved.

Optional: Work Offline In This Browser on the sign-in screen gives you a list kept on this device. When you're back online, Push To Live on each task moves it into your Personal list.

02Your Lists

You have two lists, switched with the toggle above the add bar.

ListWhat's in itWho sees it
PersonalYour own tasks, plus tasks from other lists where you own the task or a subtaskYou, your Team Leaders and the managers
TeamEvery personal task of the people in the departments you lead, plus MGMT tasks they own parts ofYou, the managers, and members whose Team view is turned on
  • If you lead more than one department (for example TC and DISPO), Team has a tab for All and one per department, each with a count.
  • Each card in Team shows its department and whose list it's in.
  • Managers choose which departments you see in Team (Team Members, Sees).

The Pill on Each Task

The coloured pill on a task's progress line tells you where it came from.

PillColourMeaning
Your TaskIndigoYour own list (shown in Team)
Name's TaskIndigoThat person's own list
Shared by NameGreenFrom someone else's list; you own part of it
Added by MGMTRedA managers' task; you own part of it
Added by MGMT for namesRedIn Team: a MGMT task your people own parts of
Added by Title Commitment AgentGoldMade by the Title Agent; ticking a blocker here ticks it there too
Task Deployment TemplateBlueMade from a task template
CSV Upload TemplateOrangeMade from a CSV file with Upload Tasks

The due date, when set, sits on the same line. It turns redder as the time gets close, and reads Overdue once it passes.

03Working a Task

Add a Task

  1. In Personal, type the task in Add a personal task.
  2. Optional: list its subtasks right away. A subtask box appears as you type; press Enter after each one. Each subtask has its own owner button.
  3. Press Add Task (or Enter). The task is yours and joins Not Started.

Status and Ticking

TaskHow its status changes
With subtasksFollows the subtasks: In Progress once one starts, Done when all are done (cancelled ones don't count)
No subtasksTap the status pill and pick Not Started, In Progress, Done or Cancelled
CancelledA cancelled subtask stops counting and the task stays open. To cancel a whole task, tap its status pill and choose Cancel Whole Task: every subtask is cancelled, and Reopen Task brings them back as they were
  • The big checkbox marks the whole task and all its subtasks Done. Unticking sets the done subtasks back to Not Started.
  • The list is grouped In Progress, Not Started, then Done. Drag the six-dot handle to reorder within a group (on a phone, press, hold and slide).
  • Rename a task or subtask by clicking its title. Changes save as you type.

Subtasks

Open a task with its down arrow, then type in Add a subtask and press Enter. On each subtask row:

  • Checkbox sets Done; the status pill picks Not Started, In Progress, Done or Cancelled.
  • Owner pill gives the subtask to someone. The task then shows in their Personal list as Shared by you, and they can work only on their own parts.
  • Details (the clipboard) opens the subtask's due date, notes and files.
  • Six-dot handle reorders it; × removes it (see Deleting).

The Buttons on a Task

ButtonWhat it does
Details (clipboard)One panel for Due, Notes, Activity and Files: switch between them with the toggle at its top. It opens on the part you used last. The button shows how many notes and files the task has, and turns red as the due date nears
DuePick a day, hour and minutes (Eastern), then Set Due Date. Remove clears it
NotesWho wrote each and when. Add with Add or Ctrl+Enter. On a task, Include Subtask Notes shows its subtasks' notes too
ActivityEvery change on the task and its subtasks, who made it and when (tasks only)
FilesSwitch between Upload Files (up to 25 MB each) and Add Link (paste a link, name optional). Everyone who can see the task can open them
BinDelete the task (see Deleting)

Under the title, "Edited by" shows who changed the task last. Hover the line to see when it was created, started, done and due.

Tasks Shared with You

On a Shared by or Added by MGMT task you see the whole task, but subtasks you don't own are blurred. You can still see their status. Work your own parts; if you own the task itself, you can work all of it. You can't move, delete or reassign these tasks.

04Leading Your Department

In Team you see and work on every task your people have, and you can add tasks straight into their lists.

Add a Task for Someone

  1. Open Team.
  2. Tap the person button (Who this task is for) and pick someone. The list shows the people in the departments you lead, Team Leaders first.
  3. Type the task in Add a task for a team member, list subtasks if you like, and press Add Task.

The task goes into their Personal list with them as owner. You keep working on it from Team, and they see it as their own.

Hand Out Parts of a Task

Give a subtask to someone with its owner pill. The task then appears in their Personal list as Shared by the list's owner. They see the whole task, with the parts they don't own blurred. This is the easiest way to split one job across people.

Find Things

ToolWhat it does
Pending (default)Not Started and In Progress together
In Progress / Not Started / DoneOne status only, each with a count
All OwnersPick a person: only tasks they own or have a subtask in. Their subtasks glow green
SearchFinds tasks and subtasks whose words start with what you type, in any case ("ai" finds "AI Review", not "Failsafe"). Matches glow green and tasks open to show matching subtasks
FilesTask Folders: every file and link on the tasks in this view, one folder per task
Expand All / Collapse AllOpen or close every task at once (on a phone, one button does whichever fits)
CancelledCancelled tasks. They leave Pending and don't count toward anyone's %

The filters go back to Pending when you switch company, list or department.

Check Your Progress

The numbers and the ring at the right of the tabs line count the list you're viewing: tasks fully done, and subtasks done out of all subtasks. The % on each company tab follows the same list.

05Task Templates and Deploy (Optional)

A template is a saved list of subtasks you use again and again. Deploy turns one into a new task in your Personal list, named as you like and tagged Task Deployment template name.

Save a Template

  1. Click your photo or initials (top right) and choose Task Templates.
  2. Press New Template.
  3. Give it a name (for example "Wholesale") and type one subtask per line.
  4. Press Save Template. Templates are saved to your account, on every device.

Edit and Delete sit on each template. Deleting a template leaves the tasks already made from it as they are.

Deploy One

  1. Press Deploy beside Add Task (or Deploy on the template in Task Templates) and pick the template.
  2. Name the task, for example "TC - 123 Main St", and press Deploy.

The task lands in your Personal list, open, with every subtask assigned to you. Hand subtasks out with their owner pills.

Add Another Template to a Deployed Task

On a deployed task, press Template on its progress line and pick another template. Its subtasks are added at the end and the pill lists both, for example "Task Deployment TC Deal Tasks + Wholesale".

Monz starts with three TC templates: TC Deal Tasks, Wholesale and Novation. TC Deal Tasks is also deployed automatically for each new contact sent from GoHighLevel, named "TC - address".

06Upload Tasks From a CSV (Optional)

Upload Tasks makes one task from a spreadsheet saved as CSV. Each department has its own upload templates; you see those for your department and the departments you lead.

TemplateDepartmentHow the file is readTask name
SOWTCColumn A becomes the subtasks; columns B and C become each subtask's note, one line eachSOW - address
  1. Press Upload Tasks beside Add Task and pick the template (it's picked for you when there's only one).
  2. Type the property address. The dialog shows the name the task will get.
  3. Choose the CSV file.
  4. Check the two switches: The file has a header row and The file has a summary row at the bottom (both on by default). Those rows are skipped.
  5. Look over the preview of the subtasks, then press Create Task.

The task goes into the department Team Leader's list with the Team Leader as owner, and every subtask assigned to whoever uploaded it. For TC that's Monz's list. The CSV is kept in the task's Files & Links, and the task is tagged CSV Upload SOW.

Need another upload template? Ask Remy with the column rules (which column becomes the subtask, which become notes, and how the task is named).

07Deleting Tasks and Subtasks

As a Team Leader you can delete tasks in the departments you lead. The hub server checks the password, and keeps a copy of everything deleted with who and when.

WhatHowPassword
A task in your own listBin, then Undo for 6 secondsNone
A task in a team member's listBin, then type the password and confirmThat department's Team Leader password
Any subtask, your own tasks included× on the row, then type the password and confirmThe department's subtask password (the department of the list the task is in)
MGMT tasks and their subtasksNot availableManagers only
  • A wrong password shows "That password is not right." Try again.
  • Shared and Added by MGMT tasks have no bin in your Personal list. Delete them from where they live, or ask a manager.
  • Deleted something by mistake? Ask Remy: a copy is kept and can be put back.

Department Passwords

  • Use the password of the department the task belongs to (the department of the person whose list it's in). A Team Leader password only works in departments you lead.
  • Share the subtask password with your members when they need to remove subtasks. Keep the Team Leader password to yourself.
  • Passwords are case-sensitive and include the $.

08Quick Reference: Who Can Do What

ActionMemberTeam LeaderManager
Own Personal listYesYesYes
See department tasks in TeamOnly if a manager turns it onDepartments they leadAll departments
Add tasks for someone elseNoPeople in their departmentsAnyone but managers
MGMT listOnly tasks they own parts ofOnly tasks they own parts ofYes
Templates, DeployYesYesYes
Upload TasksTheir department's templatesTheir departments' templatesAll templates
Delete own tasksYes, with UndoYes, with UndoYes, with Undo
Delete others' tasksNoTeam Leader passwordTeam Leader password (Remy: confirm; Brandy: her own password)
Remove subtasksSubtask passwordSubtask passwordSubtask password, or confirm on MGMT tasks
Team Members (roles, departments, access)NoNoYes

Something looks wrong? Reload the page first (Ctrl+Shift+R on a computer, pull down on a phone), then ask a manager.

manager.html:
This guide is for managers: every list, the people settings, deleting, and running the hub. Team members and Team Leaders have their own guides; share this one with managers only, since it covers admin settings.

01Getting Started

Open hub.totalchb.com and sign in with your manager Google account. Brandy and Remy can use their @totalchb.com or @kpidriver.com login; both open the same lists.

  1. Tap Sign In With Google and pick your account.
  2. The hub opens on MGMT. The clock beside the logo glows green (Live) while every change is saving for the whole team.
Part of the headerWhat it does
Live clock, beside the logoHub time, Eastern. Every date in the hub uses it. Its colour shows whether changes are saved (see below); click it for the details
TCHB / KPI DRIVER, in the middleSwitch company boards, each with its % done
Active pillHow many people are in the hub now. Click it to see who, and whether on phone or desktop
Sun / moonLight or dark theme; remembered on this device
Your photo or initialsOpens your menu: My Settings, Task Templates, Team Members, Help and Sign Out

The header stays at the top as you scroll, and the tabs line under the title stays just below it.

Help, in your photo menu, opens the guide for each person's role inside the hub: the User Guide for members, the Team Leader Guide for Team Leaders, and this guide for managers.

Open and Download at the top of Help give the guide as a PDF. A Team Leader's or manager's own copy ends with a page of their delete passwords. Managers can also open the User Guide and the Team Leader Guide there, without passwords, to send to someone new.

Live clockMeaning
Green, glowingLive: connected; every change is saved for everyone
BlueSaving…: a change is on its way
RedNot Saved: a change failed. Click the clock: Retry Now if it is waiting for a connection, otherwise redo the change
GrayLocal Only: saved on this device only; reload to reconnect

Click the clock any time to see when the last change was saved.

02Your Lists

Managers switch between three lists with the toggle above the add bar.

ListWhat's in itWho sees it
MGMTTasks the managers shareManagers. Members see only the MGMT tasks they own parts of, in their own list
TeamEvery person's personal tasks, by department, plus MGMT tasks members own parts ofManagers (all departments); Team Leaders (departments they lead); members with Team view on (their department)
PersonalYour own tasksOnly you; managers can't see each other's
OfflineTasks made with Work Offline on this device, not pushed yetWhoever uses this device; shown only while there are some

Team has a tab for All and one per department (TC, DISPO, ACQ, OPS), each with a count. Each card shows its department and whose list it's in. A person's tasks belong to their main department; a MGMT task belongs to the departments of the people on it.

The Pill on Each Task

PillColourMeaning
Name's Task / Your TaskIndigoFrom that person's own list (shown in Team)
Shared by NameGreenFrom someone else's list; the viewer owns part of it
Added by MGMT / Added by MGMT for namesRedA MGMT task (in Team: the members who own parts of it)
Added by Title Commitment AgentGoldMade by the Title Agent, with Open In Title Agent beside it
Task Deployment TemplateBlueMade from a task template (by hand or by GHL)
CSV Upload TemplateOrangeMade from a CSV file with Upload Tasks

The due date sits in the same row. It turns redder as the time gets close, and reads Overdue once it passes.

03Adding Tasks

New tasks go into the list you're viewing.

ListHow to addWhere it lands
MGMTType in Add a MGMT task, tap Assign to pick an owner, list subtasks (each with its own owner), press Add TaskMGMT. Anyone (not a manager) who owns the task or a subtask also gets it in their list as Added by MGMT
TeamTap the person button and pick anyone who isn't a manager, then type the task and press Add TaskThat person's list, with them as owner
PersonalType in Add a personal task and press Add TaskYour list, with you as owner
  • Owner lists show Managers first, then each department with Team Leaders first. Other holds older names with no login.
  • Push To MGMT under one of your personal tasks moves it into MGMT and out of your list. There's no button to move it back.

How Members See MGMT Tasks

  • They see the whole task. Subtasks owned by others are blurred and can't be clicked, but show their status.
  • They work their own subtasks; if they own the main task, they can work all of it.
  • They can't delete, move or reassign it. Only what they own counts toward their %.

04Working a Task

  • Status: a task with subtasks follows them (In Progress once one starts, Done when all are done; cancelled ones don't count). A task with no subtasks has a status pill: Not Started, In Progress, Done or Cancelled.
  • Checkbox: marks the whole task and its subtasks Done; unticking sets the done subtasks back to Not Started.
  • Order: grouped In Progress, Not Started, Done. Drag the six-dot handle within a group.
  • Subtasks: open with the down arrow; add in Add a subtask and press Enter. Each has a checkbox, status pill, owner pill, a Details button (due date, notes and files) and ×.
  • "Edited by" under the title shows who changed it last; hover for created, started, done and due dates.

Cancelled: pick it on a subtask's status pill to drop that subtask without closing the task. To cancel a whole task, tap its status pill and choose Cancel Whole Task: every subtask is cancelled, and Reopen Task brings them back as they were. Cancelled items don't count toward anyone's % and sit under the Cancelled filter.

ButtonWhat it does
Details (clipboard)One panel for Due, Notes, Activity and Files, switched with the toggle at its top; it opens on the part you used last. The button shows the notes + files count and turns red as the due date nears. Subtasks get Due, Notes and Files
DueDue Date in Eastern time; Set Due Date or Remove
NotesWho wrote each and when. Include Subtask Notes on a task shows its subtasks' notes too. Notes on a member's task are a good place for instructions

09Task Templates, Deploy and the GHL Webhook (Optional)

Everyone, managers included, can keep templates: saved lists of subtasks.

  1. Click your photo and choose Task Templates, then press New Template.
  2. Name it, type one subtask per line, and press Save Template. Edit and Delete sit on each one.
  3. Press Deploy beside Add Task, pick a template and name the task. It lands in your Personal list with every subtask assigned to you, tagged Task Deployment template.
  4. On a deployed task, + Template on its progress line adds another template's subtasks; the pill then lists both.

Templates are personal; managers can read anyone's (used by Login As User to check them). Monz starts with TC Deal Tasks, Wholesale and Novation.

GHL: TC Deal Tasks for Each New Contact

A GoHighLevel workflow sends each new contact to the hub, which deploys Monz's TC Deal Tasks into her list.

  • Named TC - address1, city state postal_code, created by "GHL CRM", tagged Task Deployment TC Deal Tasks.
  • One task per contact: if GHL sends the same contact again, it is skipped.
  • The subtasks follow Monz's saved TC Deal Tasks, so editing that template changes what GHL deploys next.
  • The webhook key is the Vercel setting GHL_WEBHOOK_KEY. Optional: GHL_DEPLOY_FOR (whose list, default Monz) and GHL_TEMPLATE (default TC Deal Tasks).
  • No task appearing? Check the workflow's execution log in GHL: 200 means created or skipped, 401 a wrong key, 400 a contact with no address.

11Connected Apps: the Title Commitment Agent

The Title Agent (title.totalchb.com) sends only Closing Blockers to the hub.

  • One task per deal, Title - address, in Monz's list, tagged Added by Title Commitment Agent with Open In Title Agent beside it.
  • Each blocker is a subtask, with a note on the action needed and its source, due at 9:00 AM Eastern.

  • The Title Agent and TC Checklist read the Managers and TC team (names, emails, roles, photos) from the hub's directory, so keep Team Members up to date.

Cancelling a blocker in the hub doesn't change it in the Title Agent; it just stops counting here.

13For Admins

How a Change Goes Live

The hub is the GitHub repo RemyTCHB/HUB, hosted on Vercel. Every commit to main is live at hub.totalchb.com in about 30 seconds; task data is stored separately and isn't touched.

  1. Edit the readable source app/app.dc.html.
  2. Run node tools/bundle.mjs pack to rebuild index.html.
  3. Commit both files and push to main.

If an update doesn't appear, check that the newest commit is under Deployments in Vercel, then reload with Ctrl+Shift+R.

Vercel Settings (Settings, Environment Variables)

Values are secrets: set them in Vercel only, never in code, chat or this guide. Redeploy after changing one.

SettingWhat it's for
HUB_FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNTThe hub-integrations service account key the server uses
HUB_DELETE_PASSWORDSDelete passwords: Team Leader and subtask passwords per department, plus Brandy's
GHL_WEBHOOK_KEYThe GHL webhook key (optional GHL_DEPLOY_FOR, GHL_TEMPLATE)
TITLE_AGENT_SYNC_SECRETShared with the Title Agent (its HUB_SYNC_SECRET)
TC_CHECKLIST_SYNC_SECRETShared with TC Checklist, for the team list only

Firebase (Project Universal-task-tracker)

  • Rules decide who can read and write what, not the page. The current rules are in the repo under firebase/; publish changes in Firebase, Firestore Database, Rules (and Storage, Rules).
  • Service account hub-integrations needs two roles in Google Cloud IAM: Cloud Datastore User and Firebase Authentication Viewer (for Login As User).
  • Data: MGMT tasks in tasks; personal lists in personal/<email>/items; the directory in meta/directory; extra managers in meta/managers; company access in meta/companies; templates in templates/<email>. Deleted items (trash) and Login As records (audit) are server only.
  • Who has signed in, or disable someone: Authentication, Users.
  • Sign-in on a new web address: Authentication, Settings, Authorized domains.
